searchDocs.title: Disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> Connection:Disconnect() → () Disconnects a function from an event.

searchDocs.title: Connect​
searchDocs.content: </> Event:Connect( f: (...any) → ()-- Function to connect to ) → Connection Connects the given function to the event.

searchDocs.title: ConnectDeferred​
searchDocs.content: </> Event:ConnectDeferred( f: (...any) → ()-- Function to connect to ) → Connection Connects the given function to the event, calls it using task.defer().

searchDocs.title: Once​
searchDocs.content: </> Event:Once( f: (...any) → ()-- Function to connect to ) → Connection Connects to the given function, upon being called for the first time it automatically disconnects the connection.

searchDocs.title: Wait​
searchDocs.content: </> Event:Wait() → T Yields the current thread until the event is activated, returns the values from the event its connected to.

searchDocs.title: Component<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Component<T> { Value: T ComponentChanged: Event<T> } ComponentChanged is read only, Value can be written to. ECS.CreateComponent("Test", 100) ECS.NewEntity() local component = ECS.GiveComponent(1, "Test") component.ComponentChanged:Connect(function(newValue) print(newValue) -- Prints 300 end) component.Value = 300 You are able to get intellisense by casting the type. ECS.CreateComponent("Intellisense", true) ECS.NewEntity() local component = ECS.GiveComponent(1, "Intellisense") :: ECS.Component<boolean> component.Value = false -- Valid component.Value = 100 -- Type error You will get an error if you attempt to run the following code. ECS.CreateComponent("Errors", 0) ECS.NewEntity() local component = ECS.GiveComponent(1, "Errors") component.ComponentChanged = "foo" -- Error component.NewKey = "bar" -- Error print(component.RealValue) -- Error

searchDocs.title: Entity<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Entity<T> { Components: number Instance: T? ComponentAdded: Event<string> ComponentRemoved: Event<string> } An entity table, ComponentAdded and ComponentRemoved return the name of the component that was removed when calling functions connected to them. All of these values are read only. Intellisense is supported by casting the type local part = workspace.Part local entity = select(-1, ECS.NewEntity(part)) :: ECS.Entity<BasePart> print(entity.Instance.Position)

searchDocs.title: _ENTITY_TAG_NAME​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> ECS._ENTITY_TAG_NAME: string Name of the CollectionService tag given to instances bound to an entity.

searchDocs.title: _ENTITY_ID_STRING​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> ECS._ENTITY_ID_STRING: string Name of the attribute given to instances bound to an entity. The attribute holds the ID of the entity.

searchDocs.title: Query​
searchDocs.content: Iterator </> ECS.Query( ...: string-- Names of components ) → Iterator Returns the ID and the value it currently has with the given components. ECS.CreateComponent("Test1", 100) ECS.CreateComponent("Test2", true) ECS.NewEntity() ECS.NewEntity() local id = ECS.NewEntity() ECS.GiveComponent(id, "Test1") for i, v in ECS.Query("Test1") print(i, v) -- 3 100 -- Only the third entity is looped over end

searchDocs.title: NewEntity​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.NewEntity(instance: Instance? ) → ( number,-- The ID of the Entity Entity<Instance >-- The Entity table ) Creates a new entity and returns the ID and Entity type, optional instance to bind it to.

searchDocs.title: BulkNewEntities​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.BulkNewEntities( n: number?,-- Defaults to 1 instanceArray: {Instance }?,-- Priority over n ...: string?-- Components to be given upon creation ) → {number}-- List of IDs of the entities created Creates multiple entities at once, if instanceArray is nil, n is used, if both are nil, only one entity is created and returned, ... is the names of the components that are given when creating the entities.

searchDocs.title: BindToInstance​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.BindToInstance( id: number,-- Entity ID instance: Instance? -- Instance to bind to, nil if unbinding ) → () Binds an entity to an instance, if no instance is provided then the current instance binded to the entity is unbinded from it.

searchDocs.title: GetEntity​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.GetEntity( id: number-- ID of Entity ) → Entity<Instance > Returns the entity with the given ID.

searchDocs.title: RemoveEntity​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.RemoveEntity( id: number-- ID of Entity ) → () Removes an entity.

searchDocs.title: ClearAllEntities​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.ClearAllEntities() → () Removes all the existing entities.

searchDocs.title: GetAllIDs​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.GetAllIDs() → {number}-- Array of IDs Returns all the existing IDs of all entities.

searchDocs.title: CreateComponent​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.CreateComponent( name: string,-- Name of component value: T-- Default value for the component ) → () Creates a new component with value T, the value given to it will be the default that is assigned to entities whenever they are given the component. ECS.CreateComponent("Test", 1000) -- 1000 is the default value ECS.NewEntity() local component = ECS.GiveComponent(1, "Test") print(component.Value) -- 1000 Different behavior is applied when the value is of type Instance. The default value of the component will be nil, entities that are given this component will also have a value of nil unless given a default instance to use when calling GiveComponent(). Invalid Values table, thread, userdata, and function will cause the function to error, these types are not allowed to be used for the value of the component.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	DescriptionInvalid value	Value given is an invalid value Exceeded maximum	There is a maximum of 32 components that can be created Already existing componnet	A component with the same name already exists

searchDocs.title: DestroyComponent​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.DestroyComponent( name: string-- Name of component ) → () Destroys the component, entities with this component will have it removed, frees up space for the creation of another component.

searchDocs.title: RemoveComponent​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.RemoveComponent( id: number,-- Remove component from an entity name: string-- Name of component to remove ) → () Removes a component from a given entity.

searchDocs.title: GiveComponent​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.GiveComponent( id: number,-- ID of Entity name: string,-- Name of component to give defaultInstance: Instance? -- Default value for instance based components ) → Component<T> Gives the component to the given entity, returns the component. If the component was created with a default value of type Instance then the default value will be nil if not given an Instance in the defaultInstance parameter. Providing a value to the parameter on a component that isn't an Instance based component will cause the parameter to be ignored.

searchDocs.title: HasComponent​
searchDocs.content: </> ECS.HasComponent( id: number,-- ID of entity name: string-- Name of component ) → boolean Checks if the given entity has the specified component.

searchDocs.title: With​
searchDocs.content: </> Iterator:With( ...: string-- Names of components ) → Iterator Only iterates over entities with the specified components. ECS.GiveComponent(1, "A") ECS.GiveComponent(2, "B") ECS.GiveComponent(3, "A") -- Assuming they all have a "C" Component with a bool value for id, value in ECS.Query("C"):With("A") do print(id, value) -- 1 true -- 3 true -- Entity 2 is skipped as it does not have "A" Component end

searchDocs.title: Without​
searchDocs.content: </> Iterator:Without( ...: string-- Names of components ) → Iterator Only iterates over entities that do not have the specified components. ECS.GiveComponent(1, "A") ECS.GiveComponent(2, "B") ECS.GiveComponent(3, "A") -- Assume they all have a "C" Component with a bool value for id, value in ECS.Query("C"):Without("A") do print(id, value) -- 2 true -- Entities 1 and 3 are skipped as they have the "A" Component end
